descriptionChirho: Aramaic verb in Qal imperative: to live, remain alive, thrive — used in acclamations and blessings directed at the king ('O king, live forever!' Dan 2:4; 3:9; 5:10; 6:7,22). English 'live,' Spanish 'vive/vive!,' Hindi जी/जीवित रह, Arabic عش, Korean 사시옵소서/사소서, Swahili uishi. All translations consistently render the basic sense of being alive or continuing to live.

labelChirho: to cause to live, to strike (Hifil)
descriptionChirho: Aramaic verb in Hifil participial form, rendered in context as 'striking' or 'leaving alive' — a causative stem carrying a distinct sense from the Qal. The multilingual glosses diverge significantly: English 'striking,' Spanish 'dejaba vivir' (was letting live), Hindi मारता था (was striking), Arabic يضرب (strikes), Korean 치시고 (striking), Swahili akimpiga (he was hitting him). The Hifil causative represents a different lexicographic sense from the simple Qal 'to live.'
